b.advice: Frame each new habit as a concrete if‑then plan (implementation intention) that links the cue (e.g., logging in) to the desired behavior (greeting an inspector in Spanish and asking a real question). Write the plan on a visible card: "IF I sit at my desk at 8 am, THEN I will say ‘Buenos días, ¿cómo va la línea hoy?’ to the first inspector I see." This makes the action automatic, reduces reliance on willpower, and helps curb arrogance by forcing a listening first step. Reinforce the plan by pairing it with a brief visual cue (e.g., a sticky note on the monitor) and review the intention each morning for 10 seconds, especially on tough days.

t.topic: Listening to diverse viewpoints in leadership
t.lesson: When a new digital asset rule was announced, the regulator emphasized collaboration with industry experts, showing that even leaders must seek input before finalizing policies. Apply this by asking your inspectors for their observations before deciding on any QC changes.
